final.title: The Eye and the Star
final.logline: Tara's third eye lights up softly as the camera slowly pushes in, and the stars behind Her twinkle, watching over the viewer.
final.hook: From the first moment the camera creeps toward Her calm, level gaze, and within the first second Her third eye lights up with a clear silver-gold glow. The viewer sees one distinct event on the brow, right at the centre of the phone screen, set against the deep midnight blue of the sky. The question the viewer carries forward is what this goddess is watching over.
final.story: One idea: Tara's name means star, and a genuine secondary sense of the word is the pupil of the eye. The clip pairs them in one image, with a watchful third eye under a sky of stars. This pairing is a devotional reflection on Her name, not scripture and not a standard iconographic scene. The glow means one thing only: Her sight watches over and protects. The 'carries across' reading of Her name is left to the caption so the clip stays one idea. Her expression stays calm and unsmiling, a protector's steadiness. Caption notes for human review: (1) the Tarapith tradition says Sati's third eye fell there (some accounts say eyeball), and the Bamakhepa account of Tara as mother is also devotional tradition; both belong in the caption, not the picture. (2) The calm-only portrayal is a deliberate series choice. She remains an ugra, wrathful-protective figure, and this clip shows only the watchful side. (3) Known inaccuracy, not a decision: the anchor's loose hair departs from the matted braid or single braid of usual iconography. It is kept nearly still, with only a gentle settle. (4) Pre-production check: confirm the third eye is clearly visible in the reference portrait. The clip does not depend on any single star being present. The sky stars are simply allowed to twinkle faintly.
final.loop: The clip ends with the glow at its fullest and the gaze steady, which gives the longest possible payoff. On replay the portrait returns to its calm starting look, so the loop reads as a gentle reset: the glow lights up again in the first second, and the eye is once more the event the viewer waits for. The framing difference from the slow push-in is small enough to pass on replay.
final.share_trigger: People send it to someone who needs to feel watched over tonight, because the glowing eye gives a clear, quiet picture of being looked after. Mythology and art fans save it for the caption fact that her name means both star and the pupil of the eye.

final.audio: A low, warm string drone under soft bell tones. One gentle bell note marks the moment the third eye lights up, then the drone holds steadily to the end.

concept.title: Star and Eye
concept.logline: Her third eye and the stars behind Her brighten together, two meanings of Her name, then ease back to calm.
concept.hook: From the first second, Her third eye begins to glow softly in silver-white while the stars behind Her brighten with it, so brow and sky read as one pair of lights.
concept.story: Tara's name means star, and a documented secondary sense of the word is the pupil of the eye. A temple tradition in Bengal says Her third eye (some accounts say an eyeball) fell where Her temple town now stands. The clip shows the two meanings side by side as parallel lights. Her brow and the sky brighten together, so the stars read as Her own light and not as something She answers. The star and the eye are not fused into one thing. The soft light that settles over Her face and reaches toward the viewer is a quiet hint of Her role as the guide who carries souls across. This is a devotional reflection on Her name, not a scene from scripture. The link between being seen and being carried through is the creator's own reading. Notes for human review: (1) the reference portrait has loose hair, while traditional images show matted or single-braid hair, so the framing stays on face and brow; (2) this reel shows only Her gentle side, a deliberate series choice, and the ferrying story is left to other reels; (3) the reference must already show the third eye, and if it does not, rebuild the anchor instead of asking the model to generate it; (4) no single star needs to be picked out, because the whole sky brightens gently and evenly, and the caption carries the devotional-reflection disclosure.
concept.loop: The lights ease down together over the last three and a half seconds and end at the same calm level as the first frame. The camera is locked, so the framing is identical at both ends and the replay flows straight back into the brow beginning to glow, with no fade or jump.
concept.share_trigger: Someone sends it to a friend facing a long, dark stretch, with a line such as 'May you be guided through this night.' The name fact (star and pupil of the eye) gives the sender a reason to choose this clip, and the line ties the clip to Her role as protector and guide.
concept.caption_hook: Tara means star. It also means the pupil of the eye. Two meanings of one name, one gaze.
concept.audio: A low, soft drone. A single clear bell tone swells gently as the brow and stars brighten, then fades gradually with the lights so the sound returns to the drone alone as the clip loops.

shots.action: Her third eye begins to glow in soft silver-white while the stars behind Her brighten gently, which makes the brow and the sky form a clear pair of lights by about second 3 against the dark. Her calm eyes stay on the viewer, and Her hair settles gently under its own weight.
shots.purpose: Gives a visible change from the first second and brings both lights in early, so the viewer does not wait for the payoff. The two lights rise together as parallel meanings of Her name, and the model can follow a simple simultaneous brightening.

shots.action: The brow glow and the starlight reach their fullest at about second 6, and a soft silver light settles across Her face and shoulders, which gives the feeling of a guiding light turned toward the viewer. Both lights then ease down together to the calm level of the opening, which makes the last frame match the first.
shots.purpose: The payoff is the pair held at full brightness for a moment, followed by a gentle return that matches the first frame so the loop is seamless. The light on Her face hints at guidance and keeps Her steady and reverent.

concept.title: The Crescent Answers
concept.logline: A faint, compassionate smile arrives on Her face as a slow gleam travels along the crescent moon of Her crown.
concept.hook: Within a second Her calm expression begins to soften, and the first cool gleam appears at the edge of the crown.
concept.story: Tara is feared as a protector but approached as a mother, and Her devotees call themselves Her children. The clip shows that turn in one small expression: the stern guardian becomes the one who welcomes. The gleam on the crescent shows the warmth reaching the crown.
concept.loop: After the smile and the gleam settle, the final frame is a calm front-facing portrait close to the opening one, so the clip repeats as a quiet new welcome.
concept.share_trigger: Devotees send it to family, especially a mother or a friend who calls Tara 'Ma', as a greeting or blessing. It also fits Tarashtami posts.
concept.caption_hook: Fierce to the fear. Gentle to her children.
concept.audio: A warm, slow tanpura-like drone with soft chimes, and a gentle swell at the moment the smile arrives.

shots.camera: Locked at eye level, front-facing waist-up framing, with the crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her calm face softens into a faint compassionate smile while Her eyes stay on the viewer, and Her heavy hair and the serpent armbands settle slightly as She breathes out.
shots.purpose: A micro-expression with a locked camera is reliable for the model and keeps identity stable. It starts the motion at once and shows Her motherly side.

shots.camera: A slow push-in at eye level, ending at a slightly closer framing with the crown centered and fully inside the frame.
shots.action: A slow cool gleam travels along the crescent moon and tiered gold and silver of the crown and then settles, as if answering Her smile, while Her gaze stays warmly fixed on the viewer.
shots.purpose: The payoff is one clear lighting change that lets the viewer feel the warmth. The push-in adds closeness without any risky hand or water motion.

feedback: virality: The hook is a calm expression 'beginning to soften' and a first gleam at the crown edge. Neither is a visible motion in the first 1.5 seconds. This is the weakest opening on a phone.
virality: A faint smile is the smallest possible payoff. Subtle micro-expressions are hard for viewers to notice at feed size and can read as a model glitch rather than a deliberate beat.
virality: The gleam traveling along the crescent is a decorative lighting effect. It does not clearly connect to the smile, so the 'crescent answers' title is only a claim.
virality: The loop ends on a calm front portrait similar to the opening, which loops fine, but only because nothing much changed.

virality: The emotional idea (fierce protector who is a mother) is the most distinctive story of the three, but the clip shows only the gentle half. Without the contrast, the 'turn' is not visible. A stern face that softens would need a clearly stern start, and the brief says the opening is 'calm'.
virality: The share trigger is the most specific (send to a mother or someone who calls Tara 'Ma'), but it is a narrow, devotee-only audience with a low reach ceiling.
virality: It is the most generic 'goddess stands there' clip: locked camera, small face change, gleam. Low novelty and low curiosity.

authenticity: 'Feared as a protector' is a stretch. The dossier supports Ugra Tara as protector from severe danger, not a goddess who is feared. The fear framing could be read as Western horror stereotyping.
authenticity: The concept never names Bamakhepa or Tarapith, so the mother claim is generic. It could be any goddess, not specifically Tara.

authenticity: The crescent gleam is described as 'warmth reaching the crown', but the gleam is 'cool' and the crescent moon is not in the dossier's iconography (only the anchor). The symbolism is arbitrary and not traditional.

authenticity: A smile on a deity who is shown wrathful and standing on a corpse is acceptable as a devotional interpretation, but a flat smile risks making her look like a generic gentle goddess. 'Her heavy hair' again highlights the loose-hair departure.
authenticity: The caption 'Fierce to the fear' is slightly flip and could read as marketing slogan language.

feasibility: Two ordered beats (smile first, then the crescent gleam 'answering' the smile) depend on timing across a single render. The gleam may occur at the same time as the smile or not at all.

feasibility: A travelling gleam along the crescent and tiered crown is a moving highlight on small, detailed metal. It risks shimmer and flicker, and 'travels along' is a sequential effect, which the guide marks as risky.
feasibility: Settling serpent armbands and heavy hair adds extra moving parts. Serpent armbands are small, detailed objects that may morph. It's a waist-up frame, so they may sit near the edge.
feasibility: The camera changes from locked to push-in between shots, again implying a mid-clip change.

concept.title: The Eye That Is a Star
concept.logline: A slow push toward Her face as Her third eye softly lights and the guiding star above Her crown answers by brightening.
concept.hook: From the first second the camera drifts toward Her face and a faint pale glow begins to gather in the third eye on Her brow.
concept.story: Her name means both star and the pupil of the eye, and the Tarapith tradition holds that the third eye fell there. The clip stages that link as one image: the eye lights, and the star above Her answers. It tells the viewer that She sees them and that She is the light that guides them.
concept.loop: The clip ends on direct eye contact with the star at full brightness. The opening frame has only a faint star, so replaying feels like the star being lit again.
concept.share_trigger: Someone sends it to a friend who is going through a dark stretch, with the message 'she sees you, you are not alone in the dark.' It is also easy to post for Tarashtami.
concept.caption_hook: Her name means star. It also means the pupil of the eye.
concept.audio: A low, soft drone with one clear bell tone when the third eye lights, and a faint rising shimmer as the star brightens.

shots.camera: Eye-level, front-facing waist-up framing. A very slow push-in begins at once, and the crown stays centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her steady eyes hold on the viewer while a soft pale glow gathers in the vertical third eye, gently lighting the skin of Her brow. Her hair settles under its own weight.
shots.purpose: Gives immediate visible motion in the first 1.5 seconds. Face-centred work with a slow camera is what the video model renders most reliably, and it introduces the eye half of the meaning of Her name.

shots.camera: The slow push-in continues at the same pace at eye level, moving to a slightly closer chest-up framing. The crown stays centered and fully inside the frame.
shots.action: The single guiding star above Her crown brightens steadily, casting a cool gleam over the crescent moon and the silver of the crown, while the third eye keeps its soft glow and Her calm gaze stays on the viewer.
shots.purpose: This is the payoff, where the star answers the eye. It makes the star half of the name visible and ends on a steady, comforting look into the camera.

virality: The loop is weak. It ends on a full-brightness star and restarts on a faint one, so the replay has a visible brightness jump rather than a seamless return.
virality: The strongest idea, that Tara means both star and pupil of the eye, lives only in the caption. The video cannot show it, so viewers who skip the caption see a glowing forehead and a star.
virality: The share line ('she sees you') is sweet but generic comfort-devotional. It does not give a sender a reason to send this clip over any other glowing-goddess clip.

virality: The third eye lights up before the star answers, but the two are 4 and 6 seconds apart and read as separate lighting effects. The causal link ('the star answers the eye') is not obvious at a glance.
virality: Novelty is low. Slow push-in plus glow is the standard AI devotional clip. The only distinctive element is the etymology, and it is not on screen.
virality: Bell tone and shimmer help, but audio cannot rescue a visually quiet first second.
authenticity: Best grounded of the three. The star and pupil-of-the-eye readings of the name are both supported (Cologne lexicon), and the Tarapith eye legend is in the dossier.

authenticity: The story says the Tarapith tradition holds 'the third eye fell there' as settled fact. The dossier says sources split between 'third eye' and 'eyeball'. It is also one temple account, not canon.

authenticity: The 'eye lights, star answers' image is a modern synthesis of the two meanings. It is a poetic device, not a traditional iconographic scene, and the story should not imply it is traditional.

authenticity: The clip is only gentle and comforting. It leaves out her core purpose in the dossier, crossing over, rescue and protection from sudden danger. A devotee may find it pleasant but generic.
authenticity: 'Her hair settles under its own weight' draws attention to the loose hair, which the dossier flags as departing from jata or Ekajata. Nothing in the clip addresses it.
authenticity: 'Guiding star' sits close to the sailor-star idea. The dossier corrected that to a modern comparison, not a textual image. The clip avoids saying 'sailors', which is good.

feasibility: Two timed shots (4s then 6s) inside a single 10s render. The rubric penalises second-by-second timing, and the clip is one continuous render, so the 'eye lights first, then star answers' sequencing won't hold reliably. Both glows may start together or the order may invert.
feasibility: Sequential cause-and-effect ('the star answers the eye') relies on ordering. Seedance may brighten both at once, or the star may flicker, so the narrative payoff is not guaranteed.

feasibility: The brightening star is a small, isolated light source. Dense or small glows tend to shimmer and flicker. A soft glow in a vertical third eye is also a small localised element that may drift or distort the facial feature.

feasibility: Moving elements: camera push, third-eye glow, star brightening, hair settling, plus a cool gleam on the crescent and crown. That is at the limit of the 'no more than two moving elements besides hair' rule. The gleam on the crescent and crown is effectively a third lighting change.

feasibility: The loop claim ('replay feels like the star being lit again') only works if frame 1 truly has the faint star, and the end-to-start jump is a hard cut anyway.

virality fix: Fix the loop by starting the clip at a mid-brightness star, or by ending with a dim-down to the faint starting state, so the replay is seamless.
virality fix: Increase contrast: a darker night background and a brighter third-eye bloom, so the effect reads at thumbnail size on a phone.
virality fix: Sharpen the share trigger with a specific on-screen line a sender can mean ('when you feel unseen'), not just a generic comfort message.

authenticity fix: Say in the caption or description that the pairing of eye and star is a devotional reflection on her name, not a scripted scene.
authenticity fix: Add a line or visual cue for 'carries across', for example a faint path of starlight below the frame, so the clip carries the saviour meaning as well.
authenticity fix: Drop the hair-settling motion, or keep it minimal, so the departure from matted hair is not highlighted.

concept.title: She Looks Up, Then Looks at You
concept.logline: Her eyes lift to the guiding star, which brightens, then return to the viewer as soft starlight settles across Her face.
concept.hook: In the first second Her eyes move upward toward the star while Her head stays level, a clear and specific change in the portrait.
concept.story: Tara is the star that guides and the one who carries across. In this clip She looks to the star, takes its light, and turns that light toward the viewer. The beat reads as guidance being handed from the sky to the person watching.
concept.loop: Her gaze returns to the exact eye contact of the opening frame, so the clip can restart as She looks up again.
concept.share_trigger: People send it to someone who feels lost or at a crossroads, as a quiet 'someone is looking out for you' message. It also works as a late-night comfort save.
concept.caption_hook: When you can't find your way, look for the star.
concept.audio: Soft, spacious night ambience with a thin high tone that swells as the star brightens, then settles into a warm low hum.

shots.camera: Locked at eye level, front-facing waist-up framing, with the crown centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her eyes lift slowly toward the guiding star above Her crown while Her head stays level, and the star brightens in response, giving the crown's crescent moon a cool edge of light. Her hair settles gently.
shots.purpose: Opens with visible motion that is easy to render, which is a gaze shift and one light change. It shows Her connection to the star and sets up the payoff.

shots.camera: A very slow push-in at eye level, with the crown still centered and fully in frame.
shots.action: Her gaze lowers and settles on the viewer, and the star's cool light spreads softly over Her forehead, cheeks, crown and silver jewelry, giving Her face a gentle glow.
shots.purpose: The payoff is the moment of being seen. The guiding light passes from the star to the viewer, which is the emotional point of Her role as guide.

feedback: virality: It has the clearest cause and effect of the three: she looks up, the star brightens, she looks back at you. A viewer grasps it in a second, and a gaze shift is easy for the model to render.

virality: The hook is a gaze shift with the head level. Eye-only movement is subtle on a phone, so the first 1.5 seconds may not read as strong motion unless the star's response is also visible immediately.

virality: The payoff is soft: the light spreads across her face. 'Being seen' is emotionally nice, but it is not a surprise. The strongest moment is the look back at the viewer, and it arrives only at the 5-second cut.
virality: The loop is only partly handled. She ends on eye contact, which matches the opening, but the star is now bright while it opens dim, so the restart has a mismatch.

virality: Eye direction depends on the model rendering a clean upward glance without drifting the face. Expect uncanny eye shifts or identity wobble, and the brief says the gaze shift is easy, which is optimistic.
virality: Locked camera for 5 seconds, then a slow push-in, is a very quiet clip. The pacing risks a low completion rate.

virality: The caption ('When you can't find your way, look for the star') is the best share hook of the set, but it leans on the sailor/guide image the dossier says is a modern comparison, not a textual one. It is fine as a modern framing but should not be presented as tradition.
virality: Weak on novelty versus other glowing-goddess clips, though the look-up-then-look-at-you structure is more story-like than A or C.

authenticity: Theological inversion: Tara is the star, the saviour and the one who carries across. Here she looks up at a separate star, 'takes its light' and passes it to the viewer. That makes her a recipient or intermediary of a higher light. A devotee could read this as diminishing her.

authenticity: The caption 'When you can't find your way, look for the star' leans on the navigation and guiding-star image. The dossier's round-2 correction says no textual source supports that image. It is a modern comparison such as Stella Maris, and the concept presents it as her meaning.

authenticity: The story's 'guidance handed from the sky to the person' is an invented mechanism. It is not grounded in any tradition in the dossier and risks mixing in a Marian-style 'star of the sea' feel.
authenticity: Like A, it shows only a soft comforting look. It leaves out the protective, ferrying and wrathful sides of her character.

concept.title: The Guardian Welcomes
concept.logline: Tara's steady guardian gaze softens into a faint closed-lip smile as Her third eye brightens once in welcome.
concept.hook: In the first second a slow blink opens into a firm, level guardian stare with the brows drawn slightly lower. The calm portrait visibly changes at once.
concept.story: Tara is the protector who guards her devotees from severe danger, and she is also the mother they call on. In one devotional account from Tarapith, the saint Bamakhepa called her mother. She is said to have appeared in a queen's dream and told her to feed him first because he was her son. The clip shows both sides in one face: a firm guardian look that eases into a faint, compassionate smile. The smile is kept restrained, closer to compassion than cheer. Her name also means the pupil of the eye, and Tarapith tradition holds that Sati's third eye fell there. So the one soft brightening of the third eye, at the moment of the smile, ties the welcome to her own story. The light carries no other meaning.
concept.loop: The final frame is the soft face with the lit third eye. When the clip restarts, the calm portrait opens into the firm guardian look again. Soft then firm then soft makes the repeat read as protector, then mother, again and again.
concept.share_trigger: People send it to a mother, or to a friend who is both fiercely protective and tender. Devotees share it as a greeting. The firm-to-gentle turn is easy to read at phone size, so non-devotees understand it too.
concept.caption_hook: Protector of her devotees. Mother to her children.
concept.audio: A low, warm string drone with soft bell chimes. One gentle swell as the smile and the third eye light arrive.

shots.purpose: The payoff is the visible turn from firm to gentle, with the third eye lighting at the instant of the smile so cause and effect are clear. Only the face and one soft light change, which keeps identity stable and avoids hands, water and shimmer.

concept.title: The Eye That Is a Star
concept.logline: Her third eye and the star above Her crown glow together once, then ease back, as the camera drifts gently closer.
concept.hook: In the first second the third eye on Her brow begins to open with a clear pale-blue light, and the bright star above Her crown starts to glow with it against the deep midnight sky.
concept.story: Tara's name means star, and a genuine secondary sense of the word is the pupil of the eye. One temple account in Bengal says an eye of the goddess fell where Her temple town now stands, though sources differ between third eye and eyeball. The clip shows Her third eye and the star above Her sharing one soft light, so the two meanings of Her name read as a pair. It is a devotional reflection on Her name, not a scene from scripture. Her steady gaze on the viewer stands for the one who sees you and carries you through the dark.
concept.loop: The shared glow rises and then eases back to the soft level of the opening frame while Her gaze stays on the viewer. The last frame closely matches the first, so the replay returns to the same quiet portrait and the light gathers again.
concept.share_trigger: Someone sends it to a friend who feels unseen or is stuck in a long night, with the line 'Tara means star and the pupil of the eye: the one who sees you and carries you through.' The name fact gives the sender a reason to pick this clip over other glowing-goddess clips.
concept.caption_hook: Her name means star. It also means the pupil of the eye.
concept.audio: A low, soft drone with one clear bell tone as the light gathers at Her brow, then a gentle fade of the tone as the glow eases back.

shots.camera: Eye-level, front-facing waist-up framing with headroom above the crown. A very small, slow push-in begins at once, and the crown stays centered and fully framed with the star inside the frame.
shots.action: Her calm eyes hold on the viewer as the third eye opens and a clear pale-blue light spreads from it across Her brow. At the same moment the bright star above Her crown glows stronger in the same pale tone, so the eye and the star read as one shared light.
shots.purpose: Gives a visible change in the first second, with the light reading at phone size against the dark sky. The eye and star glowing together show both meanings of Her name in a single glance, and a single soft event holds up better in rendering than an ordered sequence.

shots.camera: The slow push-in continues at the same gentle pace at eye level and settles on a framing only slightly closer than the opening. The crown stays centered and fully framed.
shots.action: Her gaze stays steady on the viewer as the light at Her brow and the star above Her crown ease back together to a soft glow close to the opening level, which returns the portrait to its quiet starting look.
shots.purpose: This is the payoff, a calm held look at the viewer that carries the sense of being seen and carried through. Easing back to the starting light makes the replay near-seamless.

feedback: virality: Hook is stronger than C. A third eye opening with pale-blue light and a star igniting is visible, high-contrast and readable at phone size, and it starts at 0 s. It is still a glow, which is a familiar trope, but it is a clear event.

virality: Loop is the best of the two. It ends on the opening light level, so the replay is near-seamless and the glow gathering again at the start feels like a pulse. The risk is that the seam is so smooth that the viewer sees no beginning or end, which works for a loop but does not add to the story.

virality: The name fact (Tara means star and pupil of the eye) is a real send/save hook and is the most distinctive thing in either concept. But it only lives in the caption. The viewer who does not read the caption sees a glowing third eye and star, so the clip needs to carry the idea on screen.

virality: The send line ('for a friend who feels unseen') is plausible, but 'the one who sees you' is carried only by a steady gaze, which is passive. Nothing in the clip reaches toward the viewer.

virality: Rendering risk is moderate: a glowing third eye on a face and a bright star in the sky may bloom or flicker, and a slow push-in may drift the crown out of the frame. It is still much simpler than water or hands.
virality: Novelty is only moderate. A glowing third eye against a night sky is common in AI devotional clips, and the name fact is the only differentiator.

authenticity: The concept is grounded in the dossier. Tara means star, and 'pupil of the eye' is a documented secondary sense in the Sanskrit lexicon. The Tarapith eye legend is real temple tradition, and the dossier's round-2 beat for the eye and the star is closely followed.

authenticity: It handles uncertainty well. It notes that sources differ between third eye and eyeball, and it calls the piece 'a devotional reflection on Her name, not a scene from scripture'. This is the right level of care.

authenticity: The 'one who sees you and carries you through' reading mixes the pupil sense with the 'carries across' sense. Both are supported separately, but joining them is the creator's own synthesis. It is plausible and reverent, though it should be labeled as a reflection in the caption, not as a name etymology.

authenticity: The share-trigger line 'Tara means star and the pupil of the eye: the one who sees you and carries you through' blends fact with interpretation in one sentence. A reader could take 'carries you through' as part of the pupil meaning.

authenticity: The clip shows only a luminous face and a star. It carries no ferrying or rescue imagery and is silent on her wrathful, cremation-ground aspect. The result is gentle and safe but thin on her fierce character. This is acceptable for one short reel, but it presents only the benign side.

authenticity: The hair issue (loose hair versus a matted jata) is not addressed, though the concept does not call attention to it.

concept.title: The Star and the Eye
concept.logline: A star above Her crown brightens, and Her third eye glows softly in answer as the camera drifts gently closer.
concept.hook: From the first frame, one star in the midnight sky just above Her crown begins to brighten in a clean silver-white while the camera starts a slow drift toward Her calm face.
concept.story: Tara's name means star, and a documented secondary sense of the word is the pupil of the eye. A temple tradition in Bengal says Her third eye (some accounts say an eyeball) fell where Her temple town now stands. The clip stages the two meanings as cause and answer: a star in the sky brightens, then the third eye already on Her brow glows softly in reply. This is a devotional reflection on Her name, not a scene from scripture. The idea that She sees you and carries you through is the creator's own reading, joining the pupil sense with Her role as the one who carries across. Notes for human review: (1) the reference portrait has loose hair, while traditional images show a matted or single braid, so the framing stays on face and brow and does not draw attention to it; (2) this reel shows only Her gentle side, with no ferrying or fierce imagery, and that is a deliberate series choice; (3) the star must be confirmed as one of the stars in the reference sky, and the third eye must already exist on the reference.
concept.loop: The clip ends on the lit state, with the star bright and the brow glow soft. The replay is a soft fade back to the calm opening portrait, so each loop begins again with the star calling and the eye answering. The seam is a gentle reset, not a reverse of the glow.
concept.share_trigger: Someone sends it to a friend who feels unseen or is stuck in a long night. The fact that Tara means both 'star' and 'pupil of the eye' gives the sender a reason to pick this clip over other glowing-goddess clips. The sender adds their own line, such as 'May you feel seen tonight', so the reflection stays separate from the name fact.
concept.caption_hook: Her name means star. It also means the pupil of the eye.
concept.audio: A low, soft drone. One clear bell tone as the star brightens, then a second, softer and lower tone as the glow reaches Her brow. Both tones fade out together near the end.

shots.camera: Eye-level, front-facing waist-up framing with headroom above the crown. A very small, slow push-in begins at once, with the crown centered and fully framed and the star inside the frame.
shots.action: Her calm eyes hold on the viewer as one star in the sky just above Her crown slowly brightens in silver-white, which makes it the clearest point of light in the sky and sets up the answer to come. Her hair settles gently under its own weight.
shots.purpose: Gives a visible change at second zero that reads at phone size against the dark sky. The star is the first light and the cause, and the clip uses only gentle sky twinkle, which the model renders reliably.

shots.camera: The same slow push-in continues at the same gentle pace at eye level and settles only slightly closer than the opening. The crown stays centered and fully framed.
shots.action: The third eye already on Her brow brightens into a small, soft, warm-white glow as Her steady gaze settles on the viewer, which makes the brow light read as the star's answer. The glow stays local to the eye and the star stays bright above Her crown to the last frame.
shots.purpose: This is the payoff: the star becomes an eye. A new light appears on Her face in reply, so the second half has its own event and the viewer feels seen. The warm-white glow is a different tone from the silver star, so the two read as two things becoming a pair.

feedback: virality: Strongest hook of the two: the star brightens from frame 0 against a dark sky, which is a visible, specific event. It is still a small light, so it may read as a faint twinkle on a phone.
virality: Clear cause then answer structure (star, then the eye) gives the viewer a reason to hold for the second event. This is better than C's simultaneous glow.
virality: The answer arrives at about second 5, which is late for a 10s clip. The first five seconds are only a star brightening and a still face, so retention may drop before the payoff.
virality: The loop is weak. The clip ends lit and then 'fades back' to the calm opening, a reset rather than a flow. A hard-ish seam from lit to dark loses the completion and rewatch benefit.

virality: A third eye glowing in 'warm-white' is a subtle change on a face and may be barely visible at phone size, especially if the brow is already lit. This is the key payoff, so a faint result undercuts the whole clip.
virality: The star must be confirmed on the reference image, and the third eye must already exist. These are dependencies that could break the concept.

virality: Share and save value rely on the name fact and a sender's own line. It is the same fact as C's, with no unique visual. It is still a goddess portrait with glow effects, and novelty versus generic AI devotional clips is modest.

authenticity: The cause-and-answer logic is theologically awkward. A star in the sky brightens and Tara's third eye 'answers' it, so the goddess responds to a celestial object. But Tara is the star (the name means star). Her eye reacting to a star, and the loop line 'star calling and the eye answering', invert that relationship.
authenticity: 'The star becomes an eye' fuses two separate senses of the word into one visual metaphor. This risks reading as a literal claim that the star and the eye are the same thing.

authenticity: The concept deliberately omits ferrying, crossing and protection, which the dossier names as the core of her story. The clip reduces her to 'she sees you', and the share trigger ('feels unseen') drifts toward generic comfort content that could attach to any glowing deity.
authenticity: The star must be 'confirmed as one of the stars in the reference sky'. This is a production dependency that could force an invented element if the reference has no suitable star.
authenticity: The loop ends on the lit state and resets by fading to the opening portrait. A fade to a reset frame feels like a cut, which cuts against the reverent, steady tone.

authenticity: On the plus side, the concept labels itself as a devotional reflection and the creator's own reading, and it handles the 'third eye or eyeball' variation honestly. That handling is more careful than concept C's.

feasibility: The star above the crown and the third eye must both already be in the reference portrait. The concept admits this is unconfirmed ('the star must be confirmed'). If either is missing, the clip fails on anything in frame 1 that is not in the reference. This is a blocking dependency.

feasibility: The two-stage sequence (star brightens first, then the eye answers) is an ordered sequential effect that depends on timing within a single continuous render. The model may brighten both at once, or the eye may glow from the start, which breaks the cause-and-answer logic.

concept.story: Tara's name means star, and a documented secondary sense of the word is the pupil of the eye.
